title: [WIP] Reassembler: use a double linked list to save fragments
description:
This draft is a first attempt to address the poor performances of
reassembler code described in #17311.
Major changes:
1) The fragments list is transformed in a double linked list, so that
   we can iterate it starting from the tail
2) we keep track of the "contiguous len" value (i.e the amount of
   contiguous data that's available) when we insert a new fragment into
   the list.

In this draft there is some debug code (disabled) that will be deleted in the final version.

About this implementation:

Pro:  it is much faster than the current one. The reference pcap used in #17311 is now opened in ony ~4s (against ~2m40s)

Cons:
* we consume more memory since `struct _fragment_item` is now 24 bytes larger (on x86_64)
* the double linked list implementation is a bit clumsy, because:
    
    * we use the same structure for `fragment_head` and `fragment_item` both, AND
    
    * all the lookup functions return a `fragment_head` element and we need to access the tail from it

Even if I tested this patch with lot of traces and `pytest` doesn't report any errors, the reassembler API is quite complex with a lot of corner cases so it is likely that I missed something...
Nonetheless, the goal of this draft is simply asking: _is that the right direction?_

notes.body:
Rather than using a double linked list (or together with the use of a double linked list if it is useful but it increases the memory usage), I think a major perf improvement could be achieved by keeping a pointer to the next hole so that you can quickly jump from hole to hole and find if the new segment must be inserted, and where. This should greatly improve the speed.
Note that I did not look at the patch itself (no spare time) so this is may be what you are doing already but this kind of strategy gave me huge gains in the past so I thought it was worth sharing the idea.
Thanks @pquantin for your suggestion! I'll wait for more comments and then I'll give it a try.

> In this draft there is some debug code (disabled) that will be deleted in the final version.

The debug code should make it into reassemble_test.c. This sort of checks must be put into automated testcase, as otherwise it will get broken sooner or later and then someone will spend a lot of time trying to figure out when it broke.

I think you could get rid of the `tail` parameter and have the fragment_head use `prev` for the tail, and then not increase the memory usage. Similarly, I think that, since `len` doesn't apply to fragment_heads and `datalen` doesn't apply to `fragment_item`, they could be combined if looked at carefully. Then you wouldn't be increasing the memory usage.

Even better would be finally making `fragment_item` and `fragment_head` different structures, because there are several members that aren't used in fragment_items at all and that would save a lot of memory on net.

How about just starting with doubly-linked list for now and handling the contiguous length in a different MR, if necessary?
If you're interested in picking it back up; if not, I might take a look.

Thanks for your interested in this MR.\
I honestly don't remember very well the details of what I was doing then :smile: \
Anyway, just to be sure I understood it correctly: even if we remove `tail` pointer and we don't use `datalen`, we end up increasing the size of `fragment_item` of 8 bytes, because of `prev`. Is it right? (a good improvements respect the 24 bytes of the initial version, anyway)

Please, give me few days to catch up with this code and all the changes done in the reassembly code in the last year. I am going to update you next week, if that is fine with you

Yes, that's right. On the other hand, if we do the long awaited work to separate `fragment_head` and `fragment_item` into two different structs, we can save more than that from each `fragment_item`, because they don't need `reassembled_in`, `reas_in_layer_num`, `error`, `fragment_nr_offset`, and several other fields.

I think after !8836 you could rename the `next` field in `fragment_head` to `head`, perhaps, if that's clearer. That change also gives some room to explore things like storing a pointer (and the offset / frag number?) of the first gap in `fragment_head`, since it won't increase the size of the normal `fragment_item`s
@johnthacker, just to be sure: storing "first gap" info in `fragment_head` should be done in *addition* to the double-linked list stuff?
I have implemented the "first gap" in !8937. The list is still singly linked but the speedup is significant for USBLL captures.
Does this essentially change the best case scenario from "reverse order in capture" to "sorted in capture", but otherwise does not modify the complexity?

Yes, from a "algorithmic" POV the complexity doesn't change.
But, in my experience at least, (most of the) fragments are usually in order, so the difference is quite noticeable in practice.
Otherwise, we need to change the data structured used from a list to something else
For USBLL captures the fragments are always in order, so the loop will always end on first iteration (instead of current always doing the full traversal).
Using the doubly linked list seems unnecessary because just storing the first gap (implemented in !8937) results in massive performance improvements.
